source.title: Universal Dynamics of Warmup Stable Decay: understanding WSD beyond Transformers
source.authors: A. Belloni; Lorenzo Noci; Antonio Orvieto

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains a CIFAR-10 CNN and reports that it did not perfectly fit the data, bearing on whether training reaches perfect fit. It does not measure the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper compares WSD and warmup cosine annealing training dynamics, not training classification error as a metric. Its explicit statement that the CNN did not perfectly fit the data is the only result bearing on V1. Other plotted losses and geometry measurements do not establish classification error.
record.test_reason: The study measures WSD loss trajectories and landscape geometry. Its statement that an intentionally early-stopped small CNN does not fit perfectly cannot establish whether training classification error is near-zero or substantial. Sharpness measurements do not test V5's stability-threshold behavior.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors find qualitatively shared WSD loss dynamics and landscape properties across a transformer language model and a small CNN. They identify overparameterization as a future research direction and note that their small CNN does not fit perfectly.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates WSD training dynamics and compares WSD with warmup cosine annealing; it does not test the claim's general gradient-training recipe or classification-error outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: For the CNN, WSD performance relative to warmup cosine annealing depends on cooldown length; the authors report that at least 35% of total training steps was needed for WSD to match it under their settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The small CIFAR-10 CNN was deliberately stopped before full accuracy and was described as not fitting perfectly; the amount of classification error is unspecified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: This small CNN remains imperfectly fitted under the selected training budget.

fits_no_version.finding: Both architectures show sharper regions during learning-rate cooldown, but no stability threshold or threshold-relative learning rate is evaluated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested AdamW schedules, cooldown accompanies increasing sharpness in both a transformer and a CNN.

record.peer_reviewed: HiLD 2025: 3rd Workshop on High-dimensional Learning Dynamics
record.problems: The CNN was intentionally not trained to full accuracy; no training classification-error number is reported. The paper uses one small CNN and does not report random initialization details or a comparison of initialization methods.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted. The loss curves, sharpness, PCA directions, and quasi-convexity measurements do not report the training-classification-error behavior named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error versus substantial error; effects of capacity, stopping, regularization, and label corruption.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization-dependent training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, divergence boundaries, and full-batch sharpness tracking the stability threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the proposed V1 limits_scope verdict: intentional early stopping and unspecified imperfect fit do not establish a qualification to a claim that already allows early-stopped small models to retain training error.

versions.untested_parts: Random initialization, SGD or Adam comparisons, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and the effects of model size or early stopping on substantial classification error were not tested.

rows.subject: small CNN (CIFARCNN2)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 for about 50 epochs with WSD; the authors say they intentionally stopped before full accuracy.
rows.value: The authors state the CNN does not perfectly fit the data; no classification error or accuracy number is given.
rows.note: The paper says full accuracy was intentionally avoided to keep the CNN and language model in comparable loss-landscape regions and to limit overfitting and secondary effects.
rows.check: Imperfect fit does not distinguish near-zero from substantial classification error. No training accuracy or classification-error value is reported, and full accuracy was intentionally avoided. The result statement belongs to Section 4; Appendix A supplies the stopping condition. Appendix A specifies AdamW, although the main text also says Adam.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.reason: The CNN did not perfectly fit the data, but the study gives no classification-error value and intentionally avoided full accuracy (R1).
